failure_definition: Pulse oximeter inaccuracy in low perfusion conditions, leading to unreliable SpO₂ estimates.
causal_mechanism: Low perfusion reduces the signal-to-noise ratio of the photoplethysmographic (PPG) signal, making it difficult to distinguish arterial blood from venous blood and other tissue components.
current_device_behavior: Traditional two-wavelength (red and infrared) pulse oximeters provide SpO₂ estimates based on the ratio of red and infrared light absorption by arterial blood.
failure_point: The calibration algorithm of the traditional two-wavelength pulse oximeter fails to accurately account for low perfusion conditions, leading to inaccuracy in SpO₂ estimates.
blocking_constraint: The limited number of data points provided by the traditional two-wavelength pulse oximeter makes it difficult to develop an accurate calibration algorithm that can account for the changes in blood composition and oxygenation that occur in low perfusion conditions.
